steps.title: A lever system
steps.body: is made up of three components arranged along a rigid bar (the lever itself - which in the body is a bone):

steps.title: Arrangement
steps.body: The fulcrum is between the effort and the load. F - E - L or E - F - L (Fulcrum in the middle)

steps.title: Arrangement
steps.body: The load is between the fulcrum and the effort. F - L - E (Load in the middle)

steps.title: Mechanical Advantage
steps.body: Second class levers always have a mechanical advantage because the effort arm is longer than the load arm. This means a smaller effort can move a larger load - the body can lift its own weight using the relatively small force generated by the calf muscles.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Remember: F = Fulcrum (joint), E = Effort (muscle), L = Load (weight) Identify which component is IN THE MIDDLE to determine the lever class First class = Fulcrum in middle; Second class = Load in middle; Third class = Effort in middle Second class levers ALWAYS have mechanical advantage (effort arm > load arm) Third class levers are the MOST COMMON in the body Practise labelling diagrams of levers - this is a common exam format
